defects.summary: Clearing large audit history removed logical records but did not reclaim free pages from legacy SQLite databases.
defects.verification: tests/audit-session-store.test.ts verifies new incremental reclamation and one-time legacy compaction; Settings exposes measured live/reclaimable bytes and isolated optimization.

defects.summary: Saved storage information and its maintenance action were vertically compressed into the lower-left corner of the Settings card.
defects.verification: scripts/verify-responsive-layout.cjs enforces dedicated wide right-side and snapped full-width storage-maintenance compositions without overflow.

defects.summary: AcoustID application keys were not normalized or validated before discovery, causing large audits to repeat opaque HTTP 400 lookup failures.
defects.verification: tests/analysis-tools.test.ts verifies whitespace trimming, the 10-character application-key contract, service-backed preflight, precise invalid-key errors, and bounded POST lookup construction.

defects.summary: AcoustID preflight rejection exposed Electron IPC plumbing and allowed the long message to render beneath fixed footer counters.
defects.verification: tests/desktop-error-message.test.ts verifies IPC-prefix removal; scripts/verify-responsive-layout.cjs injects an oversized status message and enforces truncation without counter overlap at all supported window widths.

defects.summary: Compare received compact audit summaries without their waveform and spectrogram payloads, leaving one or both measured visual panels blank while decoded null analysis completed separately.
defects.verification: scripts/verify-comparison-visuals.cjs loads two compacted audit records, hydrates both full records independently, and requires painted File A, File B, difference, and residual canvases plus both waveform paths; tests/full-track-comparison.test.ts rejects false equivalence from an uncorrelated short overlap.

defects.summary: AcoustID enablement, the personal API key, and MusicBrainz enrichment existed only in renderer memory and reset whenever Audio-V closed.
defects.verification: tests/external-identity-preferences.test.ts verifies encrypted restart restoration, explicit clearing, and refusal of plaintext fallback; scripts/verify-identity-preferences.cjs verifies both enabled controls and the protected key restore into the Settings UI without overflow.

defects.summary: Album ReplayGain incorrectly rejected digital album groups above the 99-track audio-CD convention and presented the supplemental calculation failure as a source-access warning.
defects.verification: tests/album-replaygain.test.ts executes exact album loudness measurement across the reported 154-track group size; the renderer now labels supplemental processing messages as audit notices and limits mounted/network remediation to actual source-access evidence.

defects.summary: A 640-file Windows audit completed every Oracle assessment but failed session finalization when hundreds of historical fingerprint requests started simultaneous 30-second timers against one serial SQLite storage worker.
defects.verification: tests/scanner.test.ts reproduces 640-file relationship finalization, enforces at most four outstanding storage lookups, verifies indexed exact-only history mode at scale, and proves a forced find-fingerprints timeout produces one supplemental notice while the full scan still completes; tests/audit-session-store.test.ts verifies exact-hash lookup and the duration/recency index.

defects.summary: A full audit could begin during asynchronous identity-preference restoration, and an isolated cached record could retain ambiguous not-requested identity evidence even though AcoustID and MusicBrainz were enabled.
defects.verification: The renderer now blocks audit startup on preference restoration; electron/scanner.ts enforces enabled identity evidence before persistence; tests/scanner.test.ts verifies a cached record transitions from not-requested to matched AcoustID and MusicBrainz evidence.

defects.summary: MusicBrainz transient 503 throttling, busy-server responses, gateway failures, and request timeouts were recorded immediately as final service errors during large identity-enabled audits.
defects.verification: electron/oracle/analysis-tools.ts retains the 1.1-second global scheduler margin and adds at most three bounded attempts with Retry-After-aware backoff; tests/analysis-tools.test.ts verifies a throttled lookup recovers to matched evidence.

defects.summary: The build dependency tree pinned vulnerable fast-uri, brace-expansion, and js-yaml releases while the default branch accepted unguarded direct pushes.
defects.verification: npm audit and npm audit --omit=dev both report zero vulnerabilities; clean npm ci applies the 5.0.9 CommonJS compatibility adapter; protected-main rules require native Windows, native macOS, Oracle parity, and dependency-review checks before merge.

defects.summary: Newly published advisories affected XML, archive extraction, URL parsing, test mocking, schema validation, and YAML packages in the development and build dependency graph.
defects.verification: A clean npm install resolves @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.15, Electron 44.3.0 with @electron-internal/extract-zip 1.0.5, fast-uri 3.1.6, Vitest and @vitest/mocker 4.1.11, joi 18.2.5, and js-yaml 4.3.2; npm audit and npm audit --omit=dev both report zero vulnerabilities, and the protected pull request requires native Windows, native macOS, Oracle parity, dependency review, and CodeQL checks.

defects.summary: A removed daily BtbN FFmpeg archive prevented clean Windows runners from provisioning the bundled analysis engine.
defects.verification: Windows provisioning now uses the checksum-pinned n8.1 LGPL static build from retained monthly autobuild-2026-08-31-13-27; the archive and extracted ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe hashes were independently verified, and the protected pull request requires the native Windows gate to provision and verify them from a clean runner.

limitations: This register establishes that no known P0 or P1 defect is unresolved; it cannot prove that an undiscovered defect does not exist.
Every confirmed release-affecting defect must be added here even when it is also tracked in GitHub.
